summary: Redwood AE + SE walked ClearBank through structured JSON output and tool/function-calling demo (JSON mode with schemas and guardrails). Showed Redwood Console flow for defining schema, returning typed JSON, and mapping tool calls (external db lookup / ticketing) via function-calling. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for pilot, security needs (KMS, audit logs, SSO), and benchmark plan. Agreed action items: share security docs, pricing, and run a one-week dedicated pilot to validate latency and correctness against their schema-driven generation use cases.
topics: Pilot scope: Dedicated vs Hosted, benchmarks, security
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (ClearBank, Head of ML), Priya Nair (ClearBank, SecOps), Tom Huang (Product)

---
00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh we are super excited to show the structured output and tool calling flow today. quick intros, I'll hand to Maya for the demo.
00:12 Maya (Redwood SE): Thanks Jordan. hey Alex, Priya, Tom. We'll start with a brief run through of JSON mode, schemas, then map to function/tool calling — some live examples. bear with me, audio may have a little lag.
00:25 Alex (ClearBank): Sounds good. Our main goals are: 1) reliably get structured responses for downstream processing, 2) reduce hallucinations when we ask for account-matched info, and 3) prove out latency for a customer-facing pipeline.
00:40 Priya (ClearBank SecOps): Also security – we need to confirm where logs live, encryption, and if there's any PII touching the hosted environment.
00:48 Jordan (Redwood): Great, we'll cover all that. quick level-set: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private/VPC options. For pilot we usually do Dedicated so you can measure consistent latency and isolation.
01:05 Maya: Ok jumping into Console — I'm sharing my screen. (background typing) In the Console you can create a route, select model, and enable "Structured Output (JSON mode)". You define a schema here — example: an invoice extraction schema with fields like vendor, amount, currency, date, line_items[]. Each field has type and optional regex validation.
01:30 Tom (Product): Does the schema enforce strict JSON? like will it reject if model returns free text?
01:36 Maya: Yes, you can choose hard validation which rejects non-conforming outputs. there's also a soft mode that logs mismatches and tries a re-generation with stricter prompt. sometimes the transcriber (sorry) generator needs a small nudge — we do auto-corrections for common issues.
01:52 Alex: What's the underlying mechanism? is this prompt-only or do you run post-processing?
01:58 Maya: It's a mix. we use schema-aware prompting plus a small deterministic validator. if it's structured output mode we include schema in the prompt and use function-calling-like annotations. we also optionally run a validator that maps to the typed schema and can trigger a forced re-call or fallback to a compat model.
02:15 Jordan: And for latency-sensitive flows we have a fast path — the runtime picks kernels, continuous batching, and KV cache to keep latency predictable. for pilot we'll show Dedicated latency numbers.
02:30 Maya: Ok demo time. I'll paste a sample request: a customer support question -> we validate intent, then call an internal ticketing tool if needed. Here I have a small schema that expects {"intent": "string", "entities": [{"type":"string","value":"string"}], "action": {"type": "string","params":{}}}.
02:52 Maya: I'm going to run it in JSON mode. (typing)
03:07 Speaker 1: [noise]
03:10 Maya: The model returns a JSON blob. see here, validated, and we map to a function call: create_ticket({ticket_type: "billing", account_id: "CB-8792", metadata: {...}}). The Console shows the function call, the payload, and we can route that to your webhook.
03:32 Alex: Does Redwood host the webhook or is it an on-prem connector?
03:36 Maya: You can choose. for Hosted customers we proxy webhooks through our secure connector; for Dedicated/Private we recommend running the webhook in your VPC and use mutual TLS or a signed JWT.
03:48 Priya: How are logs stored? we can't have full transcripts with PII in long-term logs.
03:54 Jordan: Good call. we support redact-at-ingest, token-level retention policies, and customer-managed KMS for encrypted logs. we can also configure no-persist for certain routes so nothing is stored.
04:10 Tom: back to structured outputs — what about nested arrays and optional fields? we have a lot of messy data.
04:18 Maya: Schema supports nested objects, arrays, and optional fields. we also support custom validators (regex, enum lists). for arrays we set min/max items and item schemas. and we have an example in the Console for invoice extraction.
04:35 Alex: you mentioned guardrails — how do you reduce hallucinations in outputs that require external data like account balances?
04:43 Maya: two patterns: 1) function/tool calling – we force the model to call a lookup function for account data, then merge the factual result into the JSON; 2) grounded prompts + caching — we cache verified prefixes via KV cache so the model has the factual context. also automatic fallback to a non-creative model variant if the confidence or validator fails.
05:05 Alex: can we see a live tool call? like lookup_account?
05:09 Maya: yes — I'll run a demo. calling lookup_account(account_id="CB-8792").
05:18 Maya: (demo output) The model produced the call; the Console shows the outbound request and the mocked response. then the final JSON output is produced and validated. note: in the demo the lookup returned last_payment:"2026-02-20" and balance: 12.45.
05:36 Priya: Are those outbound requests captured in audit logs? we need to see who called what and when.
05:41 Jordan: yes, every tool/function call, route invocation, and model version is logged with timestamps and request ids. audit exports are available and can be pushed to your SIEM.
05:52 Tom: what if the function throws an error or times out?
05:55 Maya: we have retry policies and a graceful fallback: if lookup fails the model can either return an "unknown" token in the JSON or call a secondary tool. you can configure fallback policies per-route.
06:10 Alex: on the correctness side, what's your approach to enforcing schema constraints for downstream pipelines — do you accept a best-effort or do you fail hard?
06:20 Maya: configurable. by default for production we recommend hard validation for critical fields and soft for peripheral fields. you can also set up auto-correct rules — for example if currency is "usd" lowercase we normalize to "USD" before it hits downstream.
06:35 Jordan: we're going to show a more advanced example: function calling that hits an internal compliance service to validate PII handling. Maya?
06:43 Maya: sure. calling compliance_check(payload) where payload has extracted PII markers. demo logs show compliance service returned "pii_level":"sensitive" so the route rejected persistence and redacted certain fields. that flow triggers an audit event and creates a review ticket if required.
07:05 Priya: ok that is promising. how do you handle key management? customer KMS or Redwood-managed?
07:12 Jordan: both. for Dedicated and Private deployments you can use customer-managed KMS/HSM. for Hosted we offer Redwood-managed KMS with BYOK options. all at-rest and in-transit encryption supported.
07:26 Alex: latency numbers? for a simple JSON extraction + one lookup what's typical?
07:31 Maya: on Hosted it varies; on Dedicated we saw p50 ~ 120-160ms for a small seqlen request plus lookup time. in our internal optimized runs we can get sub-100ms for very small payloads. but plus external tool latency — if your lookup is in your VPC that adds whatever network cost you have.
07:52 Alex: we need to benchmark — our SLAs are 200ms p95 for the live pipeline.
07:58 Maya: we'll run a pilot on Dedicated to measure p95 against your dataset. we'll also instrument per-route tracing so you can see per-token breakdown.
08:10 Tom: question: do you support function chaining? e.g., model returns a call to lookup, then based on results call create_ticket or escalate?
08:18 Maya: yes, the Console supports orchestrated flows and simple chaining. you can model a DAG of tool calls or embed the logic in a small orchestrator lambda. we support explicit function responses that the runtime can interpret and trigger the next step.
08:33 Alex: any limitations on external connectors? we use Snowflake and a homegrown internal API.
08:38 Maya: we have native integrations (Snowflake, BigQuery) and a webhook/connector pattern for custom APIs. for Private customers we provide an on-prem connector binary if you need no egress.
08:50 Priya: audit and compliance again — is there an easy export of audit logs to our SIEM?
08:55 Jordan: yes, we can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or push to an S3 export. we also provide structured audit events with request id, route, model version, function call metadata, and redaction markers.
09:08 Alex: can you show the SDK example for invoking structured output?
09:12 Maya: sure. (types) here's a curl/SDK snippet where you pass headers, model, route_id, and the schema. response returns JSON with top-level fields and a _validation_status. if _validation_status is failed we surface the errors in metadata.
09:30 Alex: we noticed the Console UI had a "regen with stricter prompt" button. does that cost extra tokens? and is it automatic?
09:38 Maya: regen triggers another model invocation so it consumes tokens. you can set an auto-regeneration policy (retry up to N times) or manual. for pilot we usually keep it manual to control cost. Redwood Optimize will later suggest optimal retry counts based on your dataset.
09:52 Tom: about cost — how do we estimate token cost for structured outputs? we have lots of small requests and token accounting matters.
09:59 Jordan: token cost is based on model + input + output tokens. structured output isn't inherently more expensive but retries and long context will increase cost. Redwood Optimize provides batching and caching hints (e.g., group similar requests, cache lookups) to lower unit cost.
10:15 Alex: for the pilot we want to test 5k requests/day, mostly short extractions. can you give a rough quote for Dedicated?
10:22 Jordan: we'll follow up with pricing. quick estimate is dependent on GPU profile and commit. we'll send a Dedicated pilot quote as an action item.
10:30 Speaker 2: [brief echo]
10:33 Maya: now I'll demo an end-to-end flow where the model calls multiple functions: lookup_account -> enrich_profile -> create_ticket. each function is instrumented in the Console. (demo) The trace shows request id and per-step timing.
10:52 Priya: you mentioned trace export. can we get full trace to our tracing backend?
10:56 Maya: yes, we support OpenTelemetry exports and can map request id to your traces.
11:04 Alex: any gotchas when mapping function outputs into the final JSON? for example mismatched types.
11:10 Maya: the validator enforces types; if a function returns string when an object is expected we flag it. you can either reject or provide a coercion rule. we recommend coercion for non-critical fields and strict for critical ones.
11:27 Tom: how about rate limits and throttling? if we burst, what happens?
11:33 Jordan: policy-based throttling. in Dedicated you can configure burst capacity and autoscale. in Hosted we enforce per-key rate limits and provide graceful 429 handling with retry-after and circuit-breakers.
11:46 Alex: can Redwood run the benchmark tool against our staging endpoint? we'd like to run realistic loads.
11:52 Maya: yes, we can run bench scripts from our infra into a Dedicated pool or run the load generator from your VPC to simulate network conditions. we'll include that in the pilot plan.
12:05 Priya: security question: SSO and role-based access for Console?
12:09 Jordan: we support SAML/SCIM and RBAC. you can lock routes to specific roles and enable approval workflows for schema changes.
12:20 Alex: ok let's talk about failure cases — what if the model hallucinates an account number and we accidentally create a ticket against the wrong account?
12:29 Maya: we have a few mitigations: 1) require explicit lookup before sensitive actions; 2) enable a pre-send review step where the system shows the proposed call and waits for human approval; 3) use validators to check account ids against your canonical list and fail if mismatched.
12:47 Tom: is there an SDK for the pre-send approval UI?
12:50 Maya: yes, the SDK allows you to embed the review UI or host our lightweight widget.
12:57 Alex: any compliance artifacts you can share? SOC2, pen test summaries?
13:02 Jordan: we'll attach SOC 2 report, pen test summary redacted, and the data flow diagram. action item for me.
13:10 Speaker 3: [muffled sound]
13:12 Maya: one more note on guardrails: we support dynamic prompt prefixes that inject customer-approved disclaimers and a rule layer that strips or flags PII before outputting.
13:25 Priya: that helps. do you support redaction rules based on regex? we have custom IDs.
13:31 Maya: yes, regex and named entity rules are supported; we can also plug in your in-house detector as a function call.
13:40 Alex: ok, last piece — monitoring and regressions. if a model update causes output format changes how do we detect and roll back?
13:49 Maya: Redwood Console integrates evals and can run regression tests against your prompt set. we alert on schema drift and can auto-roll back to a pinned model version. Redwood Optimize also suggests model/quantization changes per workload.
14:05 Jordan: wrapping up — we propose a 1-week dedicated pilot: import a sample of your requests, run the bench, validate p95 and schema accuracy. next steps are in the action items.
14:20 Alex: sounds good. Priya, Tom any final concerns?
14:24 Priya: just to confirm, we need the security docs and proof of KMS options.
14:29 Tom: and the pricing + pilot details.
14:32 Jordan: we'll send both. thanks everyone.
14:36 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with a quick recording and the demo artifacts (links to console screenshots and benchmark plan).
14:42 Alex: appreciate it — talk soon.
14:45 [call ends]
